bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge RTL, a fatal alert (alert_fatal_i / alert_fatal_o) did not clear the AES status and trigger registers. aes_control continued to drive idle, stall, output_lost, output_valid, input_ready, and the trigger write-enables from the normal FSM/status-tracking paths even when alert_fatal_i was asserted, so software could observe internal state (e.g. idle, input_ready, stall, pending triggers) after a fatal alert. In aes_core, the recoverable shadow-register-error status bit was also not cleared on a fatal alert, violating the spec requirement that a fatal alert clear all status and trigger bits.
bug_info.fix_hint: Create internal status/trigger signals in aes_control and gate the final hw2reg status/trigger outputs with alert_fatal_i: when a fatal alert is asserted, assert the write-enables and drive the data values to zero so the register bits are cleared. Also make the recoverable alert status bit in aes_core self-clearing on alert_fatal_o by ORing alert_fatal_o into its write-enable and gating its data with ~alert_fatal_o.
